name: algebraic-data-type
intent: Model a closed sum of product-shaped alternatives: each value is exactly one constructor or case, and each case carries only its own fields, so legal states are explicit and eliminators can be checked exhaustively.
problem: Code often encodes mutually exclusive shapes as a tag beside optional or nullable fields, or as an open hierarchy. That representation admits tag/payload mismatches, forces callers to rediscover legal combinations, and lets a newly added case fall through silently; a sum-of-products type ties each case to its product payload and lets matchers be checked.
context: Applies where the variant set is known and small enough to close: domain values and state machines, ASTs and protocol payloads, command/message bodies, parser and interpreter results. It is most effective in languages with value semantics and pattern matching, where the compiler also proves match coverage; in languages without a closed-set type the same design is an emulation whose closure is enforced by convention, a linter or a type checker rather than by the language.
benefits: Illegal states become unrepresentable: a value always carries exactly one variant's payload, so 'tag says circle but the radius is missing' cannot be constructed.
Coverage is checked: exhaustive elimination turns 'forgot a case' into a compile-time, lint or type-checker error instead of a runtime fallthrough.
Values are self-describing and serialisable: the tag is data, so encoding, decoding and equality are mechanical instead of spread across a class hierarchy.
Adding an operation is cheap and local: functions over the value compose without touching the variants, keeping behaviour outside the data (the dual of the inheritance-heavy alternative).
Tests are simple: each variant is a plain constructor, so a test builds the exact state it needs and there are no partially-initialised objects to work around.
Immutability is the natural default, which removes aliasing and mutation-ordering bugs from the model.

Refactoring safety: when a new variant is added, the compiler surfaces every exhaustive match site that must be updated, turning a silent runtime hazard into a compile-time error with an explicit fix list.
Domain semantics are explicit in the type: the closed set of variants documents the valid states; no Javadoc or convention is needed to explain which fields are populated when.
tradeoffs: The variant set is closed: adding a variant is a breaking change for every consumer that matches on the type, and Java even throws MatchException at run time if a compiled switch was considered exhaustive while the sealed hierarchy gained a permitted subtype later.
When operations live inside the variants, adding a new operation means editing every variant; where operations change more often than variants, polymorphic dispatch or a Visitor is the better fit.
Payloads are boxed in languages without value-typed unions (Java records, C# union declarations that store object?, Python dataclasses, JS objects), so variants in hot loops cost allocation.
Near-duplicate variant sets proliferate (OrderState, PaymentState, JobState ...) and every conversion between them needs its own total match to stay exhaustive.
In dynamic or erased languages the tag is unverified data: malformed input produces a missed branch at run time instead of a type error unless the value is validated at the boundary first.
In languages with a 256-case JVM limit (Java pattern matching), very large variant sets cannot use standard exhaustiveness checking.
Checked exceptions cannot be thrown from within pattern match arms in Java without extending every function type with a generic Throwable bound.

participants.responsibility: The closed type itself: a value of it is exactly one of its variants; it owns the variant set and is the type callers pass around.
One alternative of the sum; constructing it produces a value tagged with that variant and carrying that variant's payload.
The fields attached to a variant, grouped as a record, tuple or struct; they are accessible only after the variant has been established.
The value that says which variant is inhabited - compiler-generated for native enums, an explicit field (enum tag, literal kind, marker interface) in emulations.
The match/switch/visit that consumes the value, destructures payloads and must cover every variant; the compiler or checker verifies coverage.
Optional factory that validates raw input and returns only well-formed variants, keeping the plain constructors total.

use_cases: Domain state machines: an order is Draft, Placed, Shipped or Cancelled, and only Placed carries a payment reference and shipping address.
ASTs and interpreters: expression or statement nodes, or a parser result (Tree | Leaf | Error) consumed by recursive functions.
Command and message payloads: one discriminated command type routed by its tag, with one payload per command, serialised as tagged JSON.
Result and error modelling: success or failure with distinct payloads instead of exceptions or nullable fields (Option/Result/Either).
Protocols and event bodies that share a header but differ in content, where the tag selects the decoder.
UI and screen state: Loading | Ready(data) | Failed(error), so a screen can never be loading and failed at the same time.

Banking and financial workflows: modelling transaction lifecycle states (Pending, Settled, Failed, Reversed) with typed failure reasons per state, eliminating boolean explosion that allows 59 invalid combinations.

Multi-step business flows with typed error outcomes: login, order processing, or onboarding flows where each step can fail with a distinct domain error, and the flow short-circuits on the first failure.
Event sourcing: domain event unions where each event type carries only the fields relevant to that event, with a shared discriminant (type field) for routing handlers.
Parser and validator results: Success(value) | ValidationError(errors[]) | ServerError(details) with exhaustive handlers for each failure category.
Rust compiler (rustc) AST and MIR: compiler passes match enum variants carrying node-specific fields, so adding an IR case surfaces every stale pass.
TypeScript compiler API: SyntaxKind-discriminated AST nodes route transforms and printers, with runtime validation kept at parser boundaries because the union is erased.
avoid_when: The variant set is open by design (plugins, user-defined types, third-party extension): use an open class hierarchy, interface or abstract base, or a registry instead; an ADT's exhaustiveness promise would be false.
You only need two boolean or nullable fields and no behaviour: a plain struct with validation is simpler than a variant type.
Operations change often while variants stay stable: polymorphic dispatch or Visitor localises the change better than editing every match.
Each case should own behaviour and consumers should not enumerate cases: prefer a sealed-case-class or class hierarchy with polymorphic methods; an ADT deliberately keeps behaviour outside the data.
You need to add new variants and new interpreters independently without editing existing consumers: use tagless-final or an object-algebra encoding rather than a closed ADT.
The language offers neither a closed set nor matching and the values cross an untrusted boundary: validate a plain DTO shape at the boundary instead of pretending the tag is checked.
The domain naturally requires a DAG rather than a tree of variants, where shared behaviour across multiple branches is the norm rather than the exception.
anti_patterns: "Stringly typed" variants: a kind string or integer with no shared type, so misspellings and unhandled values surface only at run time.
Partial matches: handling the variants you know and letting the rest fall through to a default that silently does nothing, which defeats the closure the pattern is built on.
Fat variants: one variant carrying every field as optional/nullable - that is a tag plus a bag, not a product, and it re-admits illegal states.
Variant sets mirrored across layers: the same union re-declared and drifting in the domain model, the DTO and the database model without a single conversion point.
Using the union as an inheritance hierarchy: pushing behaviour into variants and then matching on them anyway, mixing the two extension axes until both become fragile.

The product-of-sums trap: nesting multiple orthogonal ADTs inside each other's variants (a product of sums) so that adding a new variant to any axis requires updating every cross product of match arms throughout the codebase.
design_principles: Make illegal states unrepresentable: encode each legal combination as its own variant instead of allowing all combinations and validating afterwards.
Closed variant set, open behaviour: functions over the value compose freely while the data declaration stays fixed.
Separation of data and behaviour: variants carry state, eliminators (functions or a visitor) define what to do with it.
Value semantics over identity: variants compare by their contents, so they can be copied, cached and tested freely.
Total functions: the eliminator must define a result for every variant, and the exhaustiveness check is the enforcement mechanism.
Single source of truth for variant sets: keep the union declaration in one module or file so the closed set is globally visible and the impact of a change is auditable.
best_practices: Give every variant the minimum payload it needs, and move shared fields into an outer record instead of duplicating them per variant.
Keep the variant declaration in one module or file so the closed set is visible at a glance and reviewers see the impact of adding a case.
Never write a catch-all arm in an eliminator over your own closed set - list every variant so a new one fails compilation; reserve wildcards for foreign or open types.
Provide smart constructors that validate raw input and return the union; keep the plain constructors total and unchecked.
Make the values immutable (readonly records, frozen dataclasses, final fields, value structs) so a variant cannot change identity after construction.
Convert between the domain union and wire/DTO shapes in exactly one place, and keep that conversion exhaustive.
Name variants after domain states rather than after shapes: Cancelled(reason, at), not CancelledRow.
Use the assertNever / exhaustive-switch trick in TypeScript to enforce exhaustiveness at compile time: assign the value to never in a default branch.
Prefer sealed hierarchies over open class hierarchies for domain modelling: the compiler guarantee of closure is only as strong as the sealed modifier.

For multi-step business flows with typed errors, prefer a sealed-monad or for-comprehension approach over deeply nested match arms, so the happy path stays flat and each failure mode annotates its step.

Avoid nesting ADTs where an orthogonal product of variant sets would create a cartesian product of match sites (product-of-sums trap); instead, keep each axis separate and combine them with a sealed-monad or explicit transition function.

When a discriminant is required (TypeScript discriminated unions, Kotlin sealed classes), use a literal-typed field (kind: 'circle' | 'square') rather than a general string or number type, or narrowing will fail.

related_patterns_notes.pattern-matching: supplies the elimination syntax for inspecting a value; an ADT supplies the closed sum-of-products that makes the cases knowable.
related_patterns_notes.sealed-case-class: is a language-specific closed hierarchy encoding of a sum; an ADT also describes the product payload and the data/operation trade-off.
related_patterns_notes.make-illegal-states-unrepresentable: is the design goal; an ADT achieves it for mutually exclusive alternatives by making each legal combination a constructor.
related_patterns_notes.visitor: moves each operation into a double-dispatch object and suits operation-heavy OO code; an ADT keeps operations as total functions over the cases.
related_patterns_notes.fold-catamorphism: is a structured, usually recursive eliminator for an ADT; ordinary matching may inspect a case without recursively folding its children.
related_patterns_notes.either: is the common two-case ADT for left/right or error/success; use a general ADT when the domain has more cases or richer payloads.
related_patterns_notes.option-maybe: is the two-case absence/presence ADT; it does not model several domain-specific alternatives with distinct products.
related_patterns_notes.immutable-object: protects state after construction; an ADT additionally restricts which variant and payload shape can be constructed.
